title: Join the Joint
statementMd:
Recently, Eva learned several advanced data structure techniques for trees. To show her progress, she asked Colin to give her a challenging problem about tree statistics.

However, Colin just gave her a very typical problem:

Given a tree with 𝑛n vertices, and vertex 11 is the root. Each vertex has an integer weight 𝑤𝑖wi.

Let 𝑙𝑐𝑎(𝑢,𝑣)lca(u,v) represent the lowest common ancestor of the vertices 𝑢u and 𝑣v.

Given two integer sequences 𝑎1,𝑎2,⋯,𝑎𝑥 (1≤𝑎𝑖≤𝑛)a1,a2,⋯,ax (1≤ai≤n) and 𝑏1,𝑏2,⋯,𝑏𝑦 (1≤𝑏𝑖≤𝑛)b1,b2,⋯,by (1≤bi≤n). Define the joint power of these two sequences to be

∑𝑖=1𝑥∑𝑗=1𝑦𝑤𝑙𝑐𝑎(𝑎𝑖,𝑏𝑗)∑i=1x∑j=1ywlca(ai,bj)

Please calculate the value of this joint power.

Eva thinks this problem is too easy, so she decided to change the problem into an online problem:

First, given the tree and the weight of each vertex. Initially, both sequences are empty.

Then there will be 𝑚m operations, each one is of the following two types:

- `1 u` : append 𝑢 (1≤𝑢≤𝑛)u (1≤u≤n) to the end of the first sequence.
- `2 u` : append 𝑢 (1≤𝑢≤𝑛)u (1≤u≤n) to the end of the second sequence.

After each operation, you need to output the current joint power of the two sequences.

However, this version of the problem is too hard for Eva, so she added an additional limitation that, after each operation, the sum of values in the first sequence will not exceed 106106. Now Eva turns this problem to you; do you know how to solve it?

## Input

The first line contains two integers 𝑛,𝑚 (1≤𝑛,𝑚≤105)n,m (1≤n,m≤105), representing the number of vertices in the tree and the number of operations.

The second line contains 𝑛n integers 𝑤1,𝑤2,⋯,𝑤𝑛(1≤𝑤𝑖≤105)w1,w2,⋯,wn(1≤wi≤105), representing the weight of each vertex.

For the following 𝑛−1n−1 lines, each line contains two integers 𝑢𝑖,𝑣𝑖 (1≤𝑢𝑖,𝑣𝑖≤𝑛,𝑢𝑖≠𝑣𝑖)ui,vi (1≤ui,vi≤n,ui≠vi), representing that there is an edge connecting 𝑢𝑖ui and 𝑣𝑖vi in the tree. It's guaranteed that all the edges in the input form a tree.

For the following 𝑚m lines, each line contains two integers 𝑜𝑝𝑖,𝑢𝑖 (𝑜𝑝𝑖∈{1,2},1≤𝑢𝑖≤𝑛)opi,ui (opi∈{1,2},1≤ui≤n), representing an operation. It's guaranteed that after each operation, the sum of values in the first sequence will not exceed 106106.

## Output

For each operation, output a single line with a single integer, representing the joint power of the two sequences after the corresponding operation.
